title: Untangling a component with too many effects

questions.prompt: Which of these does NOT belong in a useEffect?

options.text: setCount(text.length) — keeping one piece of state in sync with another
window.addEventListener("resize", onResize) with a cleanup
inputRef.current.focus() on mount
Opening a websocket for the current room id

questions.explanation: An effect synchronizes your component with something *outside* React. `count` is computable from `text` during render (`const count = text.length`), so an effect just adds a second render and a chance to desync. The other three all reach outside React — the DOM, the window, the network — and are exactly what effects are for.

questions.prompt: What does `useEffect(() => { setText(description); })` — no dependency array — do?

options.text: Runs after every render, so it overwrites whatever the user typed on the next render
Runs once on mount, like passing []
Runs only when `description` changes — React infers the deps
Never runs; a missing array disables the effect

questions.explanation: No array means "after every render." React never infers dependencies at runtime (the lint rule does that at build time). Here that makes the field unusable: type a character, the render that follows re-runs the effect and resets `text` back to the prop.

questions.prompt: A form's local draft state must reset when the parent selects a *different* record. What's the idiomatic fix?

options.text: Give the component a key: <Editor key={record.id} … /> so React remounts it with fresh state
An effect on [record.id] that calls setDraft(record.description)
An effect with no dependency array so it always matches the prop
Call a forceUpdate() to flush the old state

questions.explanation: A changed `key` tells React "this is a different component instance" — all state is discarded and re-initialized from props, with no effect and no intermediate render showing the previous record's text. The `[record.id]` effect is the common runner-up: it works, but it renders once with stale data first and is easy to break later. The no-deps version clobbers typing on every render.

options.text: It adds a new listener after every render and removes none, so one resize runs the handler many times (and keeps running after unmount)
Nothing — the browser de-duplicates identical resize listeners
React throws because effects can't touch window
It only ever registers once, because the effect body is identical each time

questions.explanation: Two bugs compound: no dependency array (runs every render) and no cleanup (nothing is ever removed). Listeners pile up, each resize fires all of them, and the pile survives unmount. The fix is a named handler, `return () => window.removeEventListener("resize", onResize)`, and `[]` deps — the browser only de-duplicates listeners that are the *same function reference*, which an inline arrow never is.

questions.prompt: In development your effect runs twice on mount. What's the right response?

options.text: Treat it as a bug report: write the cleanup so running the effect twice is harmless
Add a `didRun` ref so the body only executes the first time
Remove <StrictMode> from the app root
Ignore it — it only happens in development, so it can't matter

questions.explanation: StrictMode's double mount/unmount/remount is a deliberate stress test for missing cleanup. An effect that's safe to run twice is safe when React remounts for real (fast refresh, offscreen/suspended trees, future features). A `didRun` ref or deleting StrictMode hides the signal and leaves the doubled subscription in production.

questions.prompt: An effect re-runs on every render because `onCommit` (an inline arrow from the parent) is in its dependency array. What's the WRONG fix?

options.text: Delete onCommit from the dependency array and move on
Wrap onCommit in useCallback in the parent so its identity is stable
Keep the callback in a ref refreshed on every render and read latest.current inside the effect
Restructure so the effect depends on primitives it actually reacts to

questions.explanation: Removing a dependency the effect reads doesn't stop it being read — it just freezes it at the value from the render that created the effect (a stale closure), so you get a silent wrong-value bug instead of a loud loop. Stabilize the identity (`useCallback`), or keep the value in a ref when you want to *read* it without *reacting* to it.

prompts.prompt: Delete the derived-state effect: compute the character count during render.
prompts.explanation: `count` was never independent state — it's a pure function of `text`. Computing it during render removes an effect, a second render pass, and any chance of the two drifting apart.

prompts.prompt: Subscribe to window resize correctly: a named handler, a cleanup, and deps that make it run once.
prompts.explanation: `removeEventListener` matches by function reference, so the cleanup must pass the same `onResize` that was added — an inline arrow could never be removed. `[]` subscribes once on mount and unsubscribes on unmount.

prompts.prompt: Reset the editor's local draft when a different record is selected — without a sync effect.
prompts.explanation: Changing the `key` makes React treat it as a new instance: old state is thrown away and `useState(description)` re-initializes from the new prop. No effect, no intermediate render with the previous record's text.

snippets.question: What number does the <span> show?
snippets.explanation: `[]` means the effect runs once, on mount, when `text` was still "". Nothing ever recomputes `count`, so it stays 0 while the input says "hello". Adding `[text]` fixes the symptom; deleting the effect and writing `const count = text.length` makes the bug impossible.

snippets.question: What does the input show right after the keystroke?
snippets.explanation: The keystroke sets "DraftX" and renders — then the dependency-less effect runs and sets it straight back to "Draft", which renders again. The user can never type. This is why prop→state mirroring is a smell: the two copies fight, and the effect always wins.

snippets.question: What number does the <span> show after those two resizes, and why isn't it 2?
snippets.explanation: Count the listeners, not the events. Mount renders once, so the effect leaves one listener. Resize #1 runs that one listener → count 1 → a render → the effect runs again → now there are TWO listeners. Resize #2 runs both of them; the two `setResizes(r => r + 1)` calls are batched into one render, so the count goes 1 → 3 and the span shows **3** (and a third listener is now registered). The leak is one extra listener per render, so the numbers diverge further with every event. A cleanup that removes the listener plus `[]` deps keeps it at exactly one listener — and the answer at 2.
